rows.label: Adjustment to proportion of anemia YLDs attributed to dietary iron deficiency from GBD (Low)
rows.explainer:
This adjustment assumes that the amount of anemia caused by inadequate iron intake estimated in GBD 2019 is an overestimate. It seems like there's very little high-quality information on the proportion of anemia caused by inadequate iron intake. We have seen one source other than GBD providing country-level estimates of the proportion of anemia caused by iron deficiency, Petry et al. 2016, which concludes that other sources may overestimate the proportion of anemia caused by iron deficiency. Petry et al. 2016's systematic search resulted in finding 25 studies from 23 countries that met their inclusion criteria. Petry et al. 2016's high-level summary of their findings:
"The proportion of anemia associated with iron deﬁciency was lower in countries where anemia prevalence was >40%, especially in rural populations (14% for pre-school children; 16% for non-pregnant women of reproductive age)

rows.label: Adjusted proportion of anemia YLDs attriuted to dietary iron deficiency (Low)
Estimate of proportion of anemia YLDs attributed to dietary iron deficiency, trials included in Low et al. 2013
rows.explainer:
Our understanding is that the proportion of anemia caused by iron deficiency varies in different populations. We guess that iron interventions don't reduce the risk of anemia cases caused by issues other than iron deficiency (e.g., malaria, hookworm, genetic diseases). That means that we expect iron interventions to have less relative impact on reducing anemia risk in populations where the proportion of anemia caused by iron deficiency is lower.

To account for this, we include a linear adjustment comparing the proportion of anemia caused by iron deficiency among participants in the trials included in Low et al. 2013 and India.

Unfortunately, we have very little information to go on for the proportion of anemia caused by iron deficiency in either the participants in trials included in Low et al. 2013 or in populations we could reach through grants.
